question: What are the three 'sources of morality' that determine whether an act is good or evil?

choices.A: Object (the act itself), intention (the agent's end), and circumstances (conditions surrounding the act)

teaching.title: Three Sources of Morality
teaching.body: Catholic moral theology identifies three sources that together determine the morality of an act: (1) Object — the act itself and its inherent ordering (what is being done); (2) Intention — the end the agent has in view (why); (3) Circumstances — the conditions surrounding the act (who, when, how, consequences). For an act to be morally good, ALL three sources must be good: 'A morally good act requires the goodness of the object, of the end, and of the circumstances together' (CCC 1755). A good intention cannot make an evil act good ('the end does not justify the means'), but a bad intention can make an otherwise neutral act evil.
